title: Cline CLI npm Package Compromised via Suspected Cache Poisoning Attack

reading.body:
An AI system deployed to automatically triage GitHub issues for the Cline coding tool was vulnerable to prompt injection attacks. An attacker could craft a malicious issue to trick the AI into running arbitrary code with access to the system's credentials for publishing packages to NPM and other registries. The vulnerability existed for over a month before being discovered.

The failure occurred in the deployment's automation layer, where an AI agent operated without human review of the instructions it received from external inputs. A security researcher discovered the flaw and reported it through official channels, but received no response for weeks, leading him to publish his findings publicly. The vulnerability would have been caught by code review, credential rotation practices, or by requiring human approval before the AI executed sensitive operations.

It is not established whether the vulnerability was successfully exploited to distribute malicious code to users before the fix was deployed.

Cline CLI npm Package Compromised via Suspected Cache Poisoning Attack

summary:
Cline, an open-source AI coding tool used by millions of developers, contained a critical vulnerability in its GitHub Actions workflow that could have allowed attackers to compromise production releases. Between December 21, 2025 and February 9, 2026, the system used an AI agent to automatically triage GitHub issues, but this agent was vulnerable to prompt injection attacks. By creating an issue with malicious instructions, an attacker could trick the AI into running arbitrary code, then use a cache poisoning technique to steal publication credentials for the VS Code Marketplace, OpenVSX, and NPM package registry.

The vulnerability was discovered by security researcher Adnan Khan, who attempted to report it through official channels starting January 1st but received no response. After nearly six weeks without acknowledgment, Khan published his findings publicly on February 9th, 2026. Cline fixed the vulnerability within one hour by removing the AI workflows and adjusting their release pipeline. The team later confirmed they rotated all credentials and found evidence that someone may have attempted exploitation, though no malicious Cline updates were distributed. Cline users are advised to disable auto-updates until the security team provides full confirmation of no unauthorized access.
